rounds.text: SMC Global Securities Ltd demonstrates compelling top-line consistency, delivering a compounded sales growth rate of 16% across 10-year, 5-year, and 3-year periods [E14, E15, E16]. This robust expansion is complemented by recent strong momentum, featuring a 21% YoY increase in sales and a 23% YoY increase in net profit [E65, E67]. Profitability metrics highlight superior operational efficiency, with the company achieving an ROE of 7.82% and an ROCE of 10.55%, both comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks of 4.89% and 5.12% [E9, E10]. Moreover, the valuation presents a stark disconnect when viewed through an EV/EBITDA lens, trading at an attractive 4.41x compared to the lofty sector benchmark of 13.46x [E11]. Market participants are increasingly recognizing these strengths, pushing the relative-strength rating to a maximum of 100 against the Nifty 500 while foreign institutions have expanded their stake by 1.07 percentage points [E42, E51]. Conceded: the business battles headwinds from negative operating cash flows of Rs -73 Cr and a declining multi-year profit growth trend [E19, E34].

The current share price of ₹114 sits right at the top of its 52-week range [E49] following a 68.5% twelve-month return [E52], yet this rally is completely detached from underlying earnings reality where 5-year and 3-year profit growth stand at -1% and -5% respectively [E19, E20], culminating in an 11% contraction over the trailing twelve months [E21]. This disconnect exposes severe valuation risk, underscored by a DCF model placing intrinsic value at ₹58 with a negative margin of safety of -96.6% [E45, E46], while a reverse DCF reveals that today's price already aggressively prices in 9.4% earnings growth [E47]. Beneath the soaring chart, operating margins have compressed by 7 percentage points over three years down to 19% [E29], and cash generation has turned alarmingly negative with an operating cash flow of Rs -73 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of -0.71x for Mar 2026 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, balance sheet leverage is rising with borrowings expanding to Rs 2,036 Cr alongside a heavy debt-to-equity ratio of 1.56x [E37, E39], accompanied by massive contingent liabilities of Rs 1,097 Cr [E62] and sluggish working capital trapped in high debtors of 161 days [E63]. Conceded: [E14] compounded sales growth over 10 years is 16%.

Conceded: [E19, E20, E21, E29, E33, E34, E37, E39, E45, E46, E47, E62, E63]. While the bear highlights profit contraction and cash flow headwinds, the company demonstrates superior structural efficiency by outperforming sector benchmarks in return on equity at 7.82% versus 4.89% and return on capital employed at 10.55% versus 5.12% [E9, E10]. The stock’s supreme relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, alongside a price sitting above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with the 50-day above the 200-day, confirms powerful, validated market momentum rather than a baseless rally [E50, E51]. This strength is underpinned by robust long-term top-line expansion, maintaining a consistent 16% compounded sales growth rate across 10, 5, and 3-year periods [E14, E15, E16]. Furthermore, foreign institutional investors have increased their holdings to 2.14% as of June 2026, demonstrating smart-money accumulation during this performance phase [E42]. Finally, the business is actively funding its future via a substantial 75.6% year-on-year increase in capital work-in-progress up to Rs 79 Cr in March 2026, pointing to heavy growth-oriented deployment [E40].

Conceded: [E9, E10, E42, E50]. While FII holdings increased to 2.14% and technical moving averages are positive [E42, E50], this momentum has completely decoupled from underlying profitability where 5-year, 3-year, and TTM compounded profit growth read -1%, -5%, and -11% respectively [E19, E20, E21]. The touted sector-beating returns [E9, E10] mask a low median return on equity of 8% over the last year and a low 12.7% over the last 3 years [E28, E61], alongside an operating margin that has compressed by 7 percentage points over three years to 19% [E29]. The heavy capital work-in-progress build-up [E40] does not offset the catastrophic cash drain where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -73 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs -118 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35]. Furthermore, this cash destruction accompanies ballooning borrowings of Rs 2,036 Cr that push the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.56x, meaning debt exceeds net worth [E37, E39]. Finally, price performance completely outruns financial reality as a discounted cash flow model values the stock at Rs 58 against a market price of Rs 114, representing a -96.6% margin of safety and negative money flow [E44, E45, E46].
